h1: Pipe sanders and pipe polishing machines — automatic, orbital and centreless tube sanders, Ø3/16″ to Ø15-3/4″
intro: A pipe sander (pipe polisher, tube polishing machine) runs abrasive belts or brushes over round or square tube to grind off rust, scale and weld discolouration, give stainless steel a satin or brushed finish and prepare tube for painting or plating. NovoTech has four kinds: the BT 114-S, NovoTech's premium-line sander with two belts and an automatic feeder for straight and bent tube Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″; the Eurofintec 141 and 144 orbital sanders, whose belts orbit the tube so straight and bent round and oval tube is finished all round without turning, Ø3/8″ to Ø5-7/8″; the Eurofintec 128 S, 128 SL and 128 DL centreless sanders for bar and tube Ø3/16″ to Ø5-7/8″ and the 228 for pipe up to Ø15-3/4″; and the 728 tube brushing machine and 143 tube-end deburring machine. Eurofintec machines are built in Parma, Italy, by Gecam. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: Which pipe sander do I need?
faq.a: For handrail, furniture and fabrication work in mixed sizes, straight and bent: the BT 114-S with its automatic feeder (Ø3/8″ – 4-1/2″) or the 141 / 144 orbital sanders (Ø3/8″ – 5-7/8″, round and oval). For long runs of straight bar and tube to an even satin or polished finish: a 128 centreless sander, two heads on the 128 DL for two grits in one pass. For pipe over Ø5-7/8″: the 228, to Ø15-3/4″. Tube ends go on the 143.

faq.q: What finish does a belt pipe sander give?
faq.a: The finish follows the belt: a coarse grit removes rust, scale and weld colour; 180 – 240 grit gives the brushed, satin finish of architectural stainless handrail; finer belts and non-woven belts prepare for mirror polishing. Two belts run at once on the BT 114-S, so a cutting belt and a finishing belt can be fitted together.

The BT 114-S and the 141 and 144 orbital sanders do: the BT 114-S head and feeder follow bends up to 45°, and on the orbital sanders the belts orbit the tube as it is pushed through the head, so elbows and frames are finished after bending. Centreless machines finish straight bar and tube only.

faq.q: Round and square tube on the same machine?
faq.a: The BT 114-S takes round pipe from Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″ and square tube, passed through flat side by side, two faces at a time. The orbital and centreless sanders are for round tube (the orbital sanders oval too); the 143 deburrs the ends of round and square tube.

faq.q: How are cut tube ends deburred?
faq.a: On the 143: the tube end is pushed into a prism against a wire brush that turns while its own axis rotates, deburring the inside and the outside of the end in one cycle — ends cut at 90° or 45°, round Ø13/16″ to Ø4-3/4″ and square to 4-3/4″.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
